record.paper_title: Some open problems in the context of skew PBW extensions and semi-graded rings
record.context_brief: Gelfand-Kirillov conjecture for skew PBW extensions
record.original_question: If A is a bijective skew PBW extension over an Ore domain, can one prove a Gelfand-Kirillov-type description of its total ring of fractions, and in particular does one have an isomorphism between the total ring of fractions of the center and the center of the total ring of fractions, Q(Z(A)) ≅ Z(Q(A))?

evidence.quote: • Study the Gelfand-Kirillov conjecture for bijective skew P BW extensions over Ore domains. More-over, investigate for them the isomorphism Q(Z(A)) ∼= Z(Q(A)).
In [2] was proved the following partial solution of Problem 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let R be an Ore domain (an associative ring with no zero divisors in which every pair of nonzero elements has a common nonzero left and right multiple). A skew PBW extension of R is a ring A containing R together with finitely many indeterminates x_1,...,x_n such that:
(i) A is a free left R-module with basis the standard monomials x_1^{α_1}···x_n^{α_n}, α_i ∈ ℕ;
(ii) for every r ∈ R\{0} and every i, there exists c_{i,r} ∈ R\{0} with x_i r − c_{i,r} x_i ∈ R;
(iii) for every 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n, there exists c_{i,j} ∈ R\{0} with x_j x_i − c_{i,j} x_i x_j ∈ R + Rx_1 + ··· + Rx_n.
The extension A is called bijective if each map r ↦ c_{i,r} is bijective and each c_{i,j} is invertible in R.

Under these hypotheses A is known to be an Ore domain, so its total (two-sided) ring of fractions Q(A) exists. Let Z(A) denote the center of A, and Q(Z(A)) its field of fractions, and Z(Q(A)) the center of Q(A).

Problem. For every bijective skew PBW extension A of an Ore domain R:
(a) Establish a Gelfand–Kirillov-type description of Q(A), i.e., realize Q(A) as a skew field of fractions of an iterated Ore extension of a purely transcendental extension of an appropriate base division ring.
(b) Prove (or disprove) that the natural embedding Q(Z(A)) ↪ Z(Q(A)) is an isomorphism, i.e.,
   Q(Z(A)) ≅ Z(Q(A)).
artifact.category_tag: Skew PBW extensions and Gelfand-Kirillov conjecture
artifact.status_search_result: Listed as an open problem in surveys on skew PBW extensions and semi-graded rings. Partial results exist: the Gelfand–Kirillov conjecture has been verified for specific subclasses such as skew quantum polynomials and certain quantum algebras, but a general proof for all bijective skew PBW extensions over Ore domains, together with the isomorphism Q(Z(A)) ≅ Z(Q(A)), has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems in the Context of Skew PBW Extensions and Semi-graded Rings
status_evidence.snippet: Lists Gelfand–Kirillov conjecture for bijective skew PBW extensions over Ore domains, and the isomorphism Q(Z(A)) ≅ Z(Q(A)), among open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Problem stated as open in a survey.

status_evidence.title: Rings of skew polynomials and Gel'fand-Kirillov conjecture for quantum groups
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum version of the Gelfand–Kirillov conjecture proved for certain skew polynomial rings/quantum groups.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for specific subclasses.

status_evidence.title: Ore and Goldie theorems for skew PBW extensions
status_evidence.snippet: Bijective skew PBW extension of a Noetherian domain is an Ore domain; the total ring of fractions exists.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of Q(A) is established, supporting the meaningfulness of the question.
